Subject: Proposed language and evidence scope for Kestrel redlines

Team — drafted suggested language and an evidence scope for procurement to review. Key points:

- Output/Title: propose adding to Order Form an explicit sentence: "Customer retains title to Customer Content and Customer Outputs as defined in Exhibit A; Redwood grants Customer a perpetual, worldwide license to any Redwood-generated models derived solely from Customer non-proprietary prompts (if applicable)" — (note: this is intentionally narrow).

- Training opt-out: add a checkbox/Order Form toggle (Exhibit A) and an MSA section: "Redwood will not use Customer Content or Customer Outputs to train, update, or improve any model used to serve third parties unless Customer provides separate written consent. Redwood may use aggregated, de-identified telemetry for safety and system performance metrics."

- Telemetry/evidence: procurement typically needs a checklist showing: storage location(s), retention period(s), who has access (roles + third-party subprocessors), and sampling/aggregation practices. We should provide a one-page Evidence_Checklist.xlsx that covers: log types (request body headers, model id, timestamps), retention (e.g., 90/365 days), and where logs are retained for audit.

I redlined the MSA PDF (OrderForm-v2-redline.pdf) and included inline comments for legal to consider (e.g., carveouts for security/replay testing). We should offer: 
  - A training opt-out toggle on the Order Form;
  - A standard evidence checklist (not raw logs) to satisfy procurement;
  - A narrow telemetry use statement allowing aggregated metrics for reliability.

If Kestrel insists on absolute prohibition of any derivative model improvements, that will be a commercial negotiation (pricing/discounts) — flagging for sales.

Ben Carter
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
